page.title: Webinar Production for Finance Companies
page.description: Learn the key decisions, formats, and production steps for finance webinars, plus tools and timelines.
page.h1: What should you decide first about webinar production for a finance company?
page.definition: Webinar production for a finance company is the end-to-end process of planning, designing, and delivering live or recorded online events that meet regulatory, branding, and audience expectations. It includes platform selection, speaker preparation, compliance review, run-of-show creation, live production, backup streaming, and post-event editing.
page.quick_answer: Start by defining the audience outcome and the format that satisfies compliance, then assign a single owner for the run of show and rehearsals.

sections.h2: What audience outcome and format should you lock first?

blocks.p: Define the measurable audience outcome and choose a format that satisfies compliance before any platform decision.

ul: Live moderated panel with regulated speakers
Pre-recorded session followed by live Q&A
Hybrid event with in-person presenters and remote audience
Series of short episodes for ongoing education

sections.h2: Who owns the run of show and speaker rehearsals?

blocks.p: Assign a single producer to own the run of show, coordinate rehearsals, and manage the backup stream.

sections.h2: Which platform and production model fit a finance webinar?

blocks.p: Match the platform cost model to your attendee capacity and compliance needs, then buy production separately.

head: Model
Examples
Typical use
rows: Per-host licences sized by attendee capacity
Large regulated audiences needing enterprise security
Smaller recurring webinars with quick setup

sections.h2: What timeline and staffing do you need for a finance webinar?

blocks.p: Plan three to four weeks from brief to live, with one producer for a simple webinar and a larger crew for hybrid events.

ul: Technical check sixty minutes before go-live
Replay delivered within twenty-four to forty-eight hours

sections.h2: What deliverables should you expect from a production partner?

blocks.p: A production partner delivers the run of show, branded assets, live crew, backup stream, and edited recordings.

ul: Branded slide template and lower thirds

faq.q: How much does a moderated finance webinar typically cost?
faq.a: West Peek Productions publishes a directional range of $2,500 to $7,500 per moderated webinar, not a fixed quote. The final price depends on platform choice, speaker count, compliance review, and post-production needs. Budget also covers run of show creation, branded slides, live producer, Q&A moderation, backup stream, and edited recording.

faq.q: What is the typical lead time for a finance webinar?
faq.a: Lead time is three to four weeks from brief to live for a standard webinar, while a repeat format can move faster. A hybrid summit requires six to eight weeks of management. Lock the platform and venue AV before finalising the agenda to avoid delays.

faq.q: Which tools help manage the production workflow?
faq.a: Common tools include Asana, Monday.com or Airtable for the calendar; Google Docs or Notion for briefs; WordPress, Webflow or HubSpot for publishing; GA4 and HubSpot for reporting. These platforms support the seven stages from intake through reporting with clear owners and approval gates.

faq.q: What should stay in-house versus outsourced for finance webinars?
faq.a: Keep strategy, brand voice approval, and product decisions in-house. Outsource moderation, member support, programming, onboarding, and reporting to a production partner. This split protects regulatory compliance while leveraging external crew for live production, backup streaming, post-event editing, and clip creation.
